name: New Mexico
tagline: Pueblos, adobe churches, lava flows and old wagon roads from the Sangres to the Chihuahuan Desert.
intro: New Mexico's byways follow the Rio Grande and the old royal road north to the pueblos, climb into the Sangre de Cristo, Jemez and Sacramento mountains, and cross the eastern plains on the Santa Fe Trail and Route 66. This chapter follows the New Mexico Scenic and Historic Byways Program of the New Mexico Department of Transportation, whose list is now published by the New Mexico Tourism Department. The state folds national, Forest Service and BLM back country routes into the same list, calling the dirt roads among them scenic backways.

programs.label: New Mexico Scenic and Historic Byways

members.name: Abo Pass Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 47 and US 60 run east from Belen through Abo Pass to the ruins of Abo Pueblo, following a trade route that began as a foot path and now carries the railroad.

members.name: Billy The Kid Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop through the Lincoln National Forest runs from the ski town of Ruidoso on past old Fort Stanton to Lincoln, the Old West town where Billy the Kid and the lawman Pat Garrett both once lived.

members.name: Corrales Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 448 runs 6.7 miles through Corrales beside the cottonwood bosque of the Rio Grande, where more than 180 kinds of birds pass through. Water runs in the acequia, and green chile roasts in the fall.

members.name: El Camino Real National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The royal road of 1598 starts at Fort Selden near Las Cruces, crosses the ninety dry miles of the Jornada del Muerto to Socorro, and goes on past Albuquerque and Santa Fe to Ohkay Owingeh Pueblo.

members.name: Enchanted Circle Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Taos the circle runs north to Questa, east to the old mining town of Red River and over Bobcat Pass, then back through the Moreno Valley past the nation's first Vietnam veterans memorial.

members.name: Geronimo Trail National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the hot springs of Truth or Consequences and the dam at Elephant Butte, the route climbs through Hillsboro and the old gold and silver camps into the Gila National Forest, country Geronimo and his warriors knew.

members.name: The Guadalupe Back Country Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 137 leaves the Chihuahuan Desert north of Carlsbad and climbs some 3,000 feet into the Guadalupe Mountains, through prickly pear and sotol on pale limestone, with a turnoff to the spring-fed Sitting Bull Falls.

members.name: Jemez Mountain Trail National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The road climbs past Jemez Pueblo and the hot springs of Jemez Springs under high volcanic cliffs, by the domed mineral formation of Soda Dam, to the mountain meadows of the Valles Caldera and on to Los Alamos.

members.name: La Frontera Del Llano Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 39 crosses the Kiowa National Grassland and drops south through the railroad town of Roy, past a string of small mission churches, to Logan and Ute Lake on the Canadian River.

members.name: Lake Valley Back Country Byway
members.blurb: NM 27 runs from the mining country of the Black Range down to Lake Valley, a mining town left empty in 1994, then follows the old grade of an 1884 railroad spur east to Nutt.

members.name: Mesalands Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Roads fan out from Tucumcari across the high plains, climbing the caprock south of San Jon and reaching Conchas and Ute lakes, and Santa Rosa, where divers go down into the 80-foot Blue Hole.

members.name: Tracks Across Borders Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the Cumbres and Toltec depot in Chama the road follows the old narrow gauge grade west to Dulce on the Jicarilla Apache Nation, then up the pine-walled canyon of the Navajo River toward Colorado.
members.note: Shown on the map as Narrow-Gauge Scenic Byway.

members.name: Quebradas Backcountry Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Twenty-four miles of dirt road east of Socorro cut across the quebradas, the breaks, through banded ridges, steep arroyos and drifting sand, between the Sevilleta and Bosque del Apache wildlife refuges.

members.name: Route 66 National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The Mother Road comes in across the eastern prairie, passes motels and diners with their neon restored, and winds through Sangre de Cristo foothill villages whose adobe churches are a century older than the highway.

members.name: Salt Missions Scenic Byways
members.blurb: Its branches follow old trade paths and rail beds, two of them out across the plains and one into the mountains, where Cibola National Forest canyons south of Tijeras hold campgrounds and picnic grounds.

members.name: Santa Fe National Forest Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 475 climbs fifteen miles from the Palace of the Governors in downtown Santa Fe into aspen and evergreen forest, past the stone-and-log lodge at Hyde Memorial State Park, to the ski basin under Tesuque Peak.

members.name: Santa Fe Trail Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Two branches of the old wagon road cross the northeastern plains, one by Raton and the St. James Hotel in Cimarron and one from Clayton past the Rabbit Ears to Wagon Mound, joining for the last miles into Santa Fe.

members.name: Socorro Historic District Byway
members.blurb: A three-mile drive through Socorro's old streets, from the San Miguel Mission to the plaza and the bronze Wheel of History, reads the town's past from Piro pueblo to colonial village and mining boomtown.
members.note: Shown on the map as Socorro Historical District Scenic Byway.

members.name: Sunspot Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 6563, numbered for a wavelength of sunlight, runs fifteen miles along the Sacramento Mountains rim through pine and aspen, with overlooks to the basin 5,000 feet down, and ends at the solar observatories at Sunspot.

members.name: High Road To Taos Scenic Byway
members.blurb: The back road to Taos climbs through the Sangre de Cristo villages, past the santuario at Chimayó and the land grant town of Truchas, to the hand-restored church at Picuris Pueblo and the adobe church at Ranchos de Taos.

members.name: Trail Of The Mountain Spirits Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Out of the old mining town of Silver City the Inner Loop crosses and recrosses the Continental Divide through the Gila National Forest, by way of the cliff dwellings, on a road bicycle racers know well.

members.name: Trail Of The Ancients Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Lonely roads lead to the old ceremonial center of Chaco Canyon, then on to Crownpoint and its monthly Navajo rug auction, and to El Morro, a sandstone bluff carved with the names of travelers long gone.

members.name: Turquoise Trail National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 14 runs between Albuquerque and Santa Fe on a route named for its turquoise, through piñon and juniper hills to the artists' towns of Madrid and Los Cerrillos, with a spur up NM 536 to Sandia Crest.

members.name: Wild Rivers Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop across the sagebrush of the Taos Plateau runs along the rim of the Rio Grande gorge to La Junta Overlook, where the Red River comes in 800 feet below between walls of black rock.

members.name: Puye Cliffs Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Indian Road 565 crosses Santa Clara Pueblo land to the Puye Cliff Dwellings, rooms carved into soft volcanic tufa with adobe houses once built along the slopes and mesa top.

members.name: Chain of Craters Back Country Byway
members.blurb: County Road 42 runs 33 miles of dirt and gravel through El Malpais between NM 53 and NM 117, along the western edge of the West Malpais Wilderness, with no water and no services until Grants.

members.name: Sandia Crest National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NM 536 leaves the Turquoise Trail and climbs through the Cibola National Forest to Sandia Crest, in what the Forest Service calls the most visited mountains in New Mexico, with sheltered picnic grounds along the way.
